bullets: What if the data has a non-numeric representation (e.g. Tennis Playing example)
Features are nominal (Low/High, Yes/No, Overcast/Rainy/Sunny, etc.)
Features with only 2 possible values can be represented as 0/1
What about features having more than 2 possible values?
Can't we just map Sunny to 0, Overcast to 1, Rainy to 2?

recreation_brief: 1. Set slide background to light gray (#E8E8E8) and draw a thin dark-red rectangular frame around the whole slide. 2. Add centered bold dark-red (#AA0000) title 'Non-Numeric' on line 1 and 'Data Representation' on line 2 at top. 3. Add a yellow (#FFFF99) circle with '27' at top-right. 4. Draw a white rounded rectangle with thin red border below the title; inside place 5 bullets verbatim: bullet 1 'What if the data has a non-numeric representation (e.g. Tennis Playing example)' (black); bullet 2 'Features are nominal (Low/High, Yes/No, Overcast/Rainy/Sunny, etc.)' (black); bullet 3 'Features with only 2 possible values can be represented as 0/1' (blue #0000CC); bullet 4 'What about features having more than 2 possible values?' (red italic); bullet 5 'Can't we just map Sunny to 0, Overcast to 1, Rainy to 2?' with 'Can't we just' bold black and the rest blue italic underlined. 5. Bottom-left: pale yellow (#FFFFCC) 2x5 table: rows P/Play, N/No Play, Out/Outlook, T/Temperature, R/Humidity. 6. Bottom-center: table with headers Y, Out, T, R; Y column values P,N,N,P,P,P,P,N; Out column filled pink (#FF99CC) with Sunny,Sunny,Sunny,Overcast,Overcast,Overcast,Rainy,Rainy; T column filled orange (#FFCC99) with Low,High,High,Low,High,Low,Low,Low; R column filled green (#99FF99) with Yes,Yes,No,Yes,No,No,Yes,No. 7. Draw a hollow red right-pointing arrow to the right of that table. 8. Right of arrow: second table, headers Y, Out, T, R; Y column 1,0,0,1,1,1,0,1; Out column pink with eight '?' marks; T column orange with 0/1 values (1,0,0,0,0,0,0,0); R column green with 0/1 values (1,1,0,0,0,1,0,1).
